subject: Spanska 4
title: Reported speech (estilo indirecto)
sourceSummary: Converting direct quotes into reported speech, and the tense shifts and perspective changes that requires.

questions.prompt: Convert to reported speech: María dijo: "Estoy cansada." → María dijo que ___.
questions.opener: When the reporting verb is in the past (dijo), the present shifts one step back: to the imperfect.
questions.explanation: Since "dijo" (said) is in the past, the present ("estoy") shifts one step back to the imperfect: "estaba cansada". This is the basic pattern of estilo indirecto.

questions.prompt: Convert to reported speech: Carlos dijo: "Llegué tarde." → Carlos dijo que ___.
questions.opener: The preterite shifts back to the pluperfect in reported speech.
questions.explanation: The preterite ("llegué") shifts one step back to the pluperfect: "había llegado tarde". The pattern: present→imperfect, preterite→pluperfect.

questions.prompt: Convert to reported speech: Ana dijo: "Iré a la fiesta." → Ana dijo que ___.
questions.opener: The future shifts back to the conditional in reported speech.
questions.explanation: The future ("iré") shifts back to the conditional: "iría a la fiesta". This pattern applies to all future forms when the reporting verb is in the past.

questions.prompt: Convert to reported speech: El profesor dijo: "Estudiad más." → El profesor nos dijo que ___.
questions.opener: An imperative in direct speech becomes the subjunctive in reported speech (often the imperfect subjunctive after dijo).
questions.explanation: An imperative ("estudiad") in direct speech becomes the imperfect subjunctive in reported speech after a past-tense verb: "que estudiáramos más". Note also that the form changes (estudiad → estudiáramos), since the perspective is now "we" who were told, not the original direct address.

questions.prompt: Convert to reported speech: Pedro dijo: "Vendré aquí mañana." → Pedro dijo que ___.
questions.opener: Both the tense AND time/place expressions change in reported speech: "mañana" → "al día siguiente", "aquí" → "allí".
questions.explanation: Future (vendré) → conditional (vendría). In addition, deictic expressions shift: "aquí" (here, from the original speaker's perspective) → "allí" (there), and "mañana" (tomorrow) → "al día siguiente" (the next day), since the perspective is now the narrator's, not the original speaker's.

questions.prompt: Convert to reported speech: Laura preguntó: "¿Vienes a la fiesta?" → Laura preguntó ___.
questions.opener: Yes/no questions in reported speech are introduced with "si" (whether), and the word order becomes that of a statement, not a question.
questions.explanation: A yes/no question in reported speech is introduced with the conjunction "si" (whether), not "que", and the verb shifts back in tense as usual: "preguntó si venía a la fiesta".

questions.prompt: Convert to reported speech: Marta dijo: "Estoy muy ocupada hoy, pero mañana tendré tiempo libre y podré ayudarte." → Marta dijo que...
questions.opener: Three verbs need to shift back in tense, and the time expression "mañana" needs to change.
questions.answer: Marta dijo que estaba muy ocupada aquel día, pero que al día siguiente tendría tiempo libre y podría ayudarle.
steps: "Estoy" (present) → "estaba" (imperfect), because the reporting verb "dijo" is in the past.
"Hoy" (today) changes to "aquel día" (that day), since we're now narrating it afterwards.
"Mañana" (tomorrow) changes to "al día siguiente" (the next day).
"Ayudarte" (you) changes to "ayudarle" (him/her), since the perspective is now third person, not direct address.

questions.prompt: What tense shifts and other changes happen in estilo indirecto?
questions.opener: A pattern to memorize so you can move smoothly between direct and reported speech.
questions.answer: Tense shifts (when the reporting verb is in the past, e.g. dijo que): presente→imperfecto (estoy→estaba), pretérito→pluscuamperfecto (llegué→había llegado), futuro→condicional (iré→iría), imperativo→imperfecto de subjuntivo (estudiad→estudiáramos). Time/place expressions: hoy→aquel día, mañana→al día siguiente, ayer→el día anterior, aquí→allí, este→aquel. Questions: yes/no questions get "si" (preguntó si venía), wh-questions keep the question word (preguntó cuándo venía) — with no question mark and no inverted word order. Pronouns always adjust to the new perspective.

questions.prompt: Convert to reported speech: Sofía dijo: "Tengo hambre." → Sofía dijo que ___.
questions.opener: The present shifts one step back to the imperfect.
questions.explanation: The present ("tengo") shifts back to the imperfect: "tenía hambre".

questions.prompt: Convert to reported speech: Miguel dijo: "He terminado el trabajo." → Miguel dijo que ___.
questions.opener: The present perfect (he terminado) shifts back to the pluperfect.
questions.explanation: "He terminado" (present perfect) shifts back to the pluperfect: "había terminado el trabajo".

questions.prompt: Convert to reported speech: Rosa dijo: "Vivía en Madrid." → Rosa dijo que ___.
questions.opener: The imperfect does NOT shift back in reported speech — it stays the imperfect.
questions.explanation: The imperfect ("vivía") stays unchanged in reported speech, since it already describes background/habit in the past: "vivía en Madrid".

questions.prompt: Convert to reported speech: Juan preguntó: "¿Dónde vives?" → Juan preguntó ___.
questions.opener: Wh-questions keep the question word but lose the question mark and inverted word order.
questions.explanation: A wh-question keeps the question word ("dónde") without "que", and the verb shifts back in tense: "preguntó dónde vivía".

questions.prompt: Convert to reported speech: María dijo: "Este libro es mío." → María dijo que ___ libro era suyo.
questions.opener: The deictic word "este" (this, near the speaker) shifts back to "aquel" (that).
questions.explanation: "Este" (this, near the speaker in the moment) becomes "aquel" (that) in reported speech, since the perspective moves away from the original speech situation.

questions.prompt: Convert to reported speech: El médico dijo: "No fumes." → El médico le dijo que ___.
questions.opener: A negative imperative in direct speech becomes "no" + the imperfect subjunctive in reported speech.
questions.explanation: An imperative ("no fumes") becomes the imperfect subjunctive in reported speech after a past-tense verb: "que no fumara".

questions.prompt: Convert to reported speech: Pablo dijo: "Llegué ayer." → Pablo dijo que había llegado ___.
questions.opener: "Ayer" (yesterday) shifts back to "el día anterior" (the day before).
questions.explanation: "Ayer" (yesterday, from the original speaker's perspective) becomes "el día anterior" (the day before) in reported speech.
